The Chinese translation is very misleading.

I saw there was another player talking about the translation issue in Chinese version. The developer changed '重新开始单人之旅', which means 'restart single-player game' to '继续单人之旅', which means 'resume single-player game' in the main menu. Unfortunately, the developer only changed the translation for single-player mode. When I exit and re-entered the game, I saw '重新开始合作模式', which means  'restart co-op game', so I hit '合作模式', which means 'co-op mode' in Chinese. As you can expect, all the records were erased and the game started all over. From what I see in the comments, it's not the first time this kind of translation problem occurs, but obviously the developer doesn't care. 

If the developer is not paying attention to its users, I am not paying for the game either. I shouldn't waste my time to play the same game all over again just because of the developer's negligence.

From beginning to end, it took less than 1.5 hours for us to complete this 2-player couch puzzle game. It does not feel like it is worth the $15 investment, since it took so little time to complete it.

It is a collection of Flash-like puzzles that are mostly very limited in how you can interact with them intentionally to require two people, even though logically they wouldn't necessitate two people. For example, in many of them you lift an object, but cannot rotate it without the second player helping. It was so frustrating requiring assistance for simple things like just tipping anything to pour it (like a watering can) or needing a second player to clip with the plant-clipper. This isn't a good co-op puzzle design, it feels akin to a forced `QWOP`-like situation where a second player is required for the most basic of control.

The controls are not really explained in most, and just figuring out how to move, for example, in the bike/coal-gathering puzzle was more a puzzle than the rest of it.

After almost every puzzle is solved, you have to create scones or tea. This feels like a stripped down `Papa's` flash game, except esp. in the scones one where you have to drop ingredients onto your scone while the physics are jittering everything so oddly, and just hope that it counts according to the rules of the game.

Grab this game on sale. We absolutely loved the cooperative adventure and entirely charming characters/storyline, but found it to be very short indeed. Finished in perhaps 2 hours, and doesn't seemingly have much replay value. My only criticism other than the length is some of the late game puzzles cause visual disturbances if you fail them on your first try, not only making subsequent tries tougher but also nauseating anyone who has motion sickness issues. I looked in Options to see if the devs had implemented something to address this and disappointingly they had not. Overall: 7.5/10, would support these fantastically creative devs again!

Excellent little game that is best played with 2 people. Remote Play Together is a bit wonky, although the occasional lagging never really spoiled the fun. Make Albert and Baxter their tea and scones and take them to the wonderfully barren surface of Mars. The game has a great atmosphere (you may punish me for that pun) due to the unity of the art style, the music and the dialogues. If you want to play a fairly relaxed puzzle game with witty characters, go for it!
